hindi: प्रत्येक वास्तविक संख्या $\theta$ के लिए माना कि $w(\theta)=(3+4i)e^{i\theta}+(7-i)e^{-i\theta}$ है, जहाँ $i=\sqrt{-1}$ है। जब $\theta$ सम्पूर्ण $\mathbb{R}$ पर परिवर्तित होता है, तब आर्गण्ड तल में $w(\theta)$ को निरूपित करने वाला बिन्दु एक दीर्घवृत्त अनुरेखित करता है। तब इस दीर्घवृत्त के दीर्घ अक्ष की प्रवणता है
solution: So in axes turned through $\dfrac{\pi}{8}$ the locus is an ellipse with semi-axes $5\sqrt{2}+5$ (along the direction $\dfrac{\pi}{8}$) and $5\sqrt{2}-5$
solution_full: Let $\alpha=\arg(3+4i)$ and $\beta=\arg(7-i)$. Then $3+4i=5e^{i\alpha}$ with $\tan\alpha=\dfrac{4}{3}$, $\alpha\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, and $7-i=5\sqrt{2}\,e^{i\beta}$ with $\tan\beta=-\dfrac{1}{7}$, $\beta\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)$.
Now $w(\theta)=5e^{i(\theta+\alpha)}+5\sqrt{2}e^{-i(\theta-\beta)}$. Take out the factor $e^{i(\alpha+\beta)/2}$ and put $\psi=\theta+\dfrac{\alpha-\beta}{2}$:

As $\theta$ runs over $\mathbb{R}$, so does $\psi$, and the point $X+iY$ with $X=(5\sqrt{2}+5)\cos\psi$, $Y=-(5\sqrt{2}-5)\sin\psi$ traces the ellipse $\dfrac{X^{2}}{(5\sqrt{2}+5)^{2}}+\dfrac{Y^{2}}{(5\sqrt{2}-5)^{2}}=1$ with its major axis along the $X$-axis.

Multiplying by $e^{i(\alpha+\beta)/2}=e^{i\pi/8}$ rotates this ellipse through $\dfrac{\pi}{8}$ about the origin, so the major axis of the locus of $w$ makes the angle $\dfrac{\pi}{8}$ with the real axis.
(The minor axis has slope $-(\sqrt{2}+1)$; the direction $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ of $\alpha+\beta$ itself would give the wrong slope $1$.)
originality_note: New: a sum of two counter-rotating vectors of unequal length traces a rotated ellipse whose major axis lies along half the sum of their arguments, so the compound-angle formula fixes the axis (way 4, hidden structure). Closest known: locus of z + 1/z for |z| = r is an ellipse (JEE 2023). Different because: the two vectors have different arguments, so the ellipse is rotated and its axis must be found with tan(A+B) and a half angle.
blueprint_concepts: Polar form and exponential form of complex number

concept_use.Polar form and exponential form of compl: 3+4i and 7-i are written as 5e^{i alpha}, 5 sqrt2 e^{i beta}, and w is factored as e^{i(alpha+beta)/2} times an ellipse in standard position.
concept_use.Compound angles: sin(A+/-B), cos(A+/-B),: tan(alpha+beta) = 1 fixes the axis direction pi/8, and tan(pi/8) is found from the half-angle form of the compound-angle results.

key_step: Factor e^{i(alpha+beta)/2} out of the sum of counter-rotating vectors; get alpha+beta = pi/4 by tan(A+B), so the major axis is at pi/8.
justification: The decomposition of u e^{i t} + v e^{-i t} into a rotated ellipse is not a routine coaching pattern; brute force gives a linear image of a circle whose axes are hard to find. Two ideas linked (polar factorisation and compound angle) puts it at average Advanced, like 2021-P1-Q4 (L3).
